title: Bronx and Harlem clubs, Irene Reid, Pearl Bailey
summary: Campbell reminisces about Brook Benton, Irene Reid, Lou Donaldson and Pearl Bailey at the Blue Morocco.

We were talking about Irene Reid playing on Boston Road, right here off 168th Street, she used sing with a group, Robert (inaudible) on piano who, if you heard him sing, sounds just like Nat King Cole. I'll tell you who else sounds just like Nat King Cole when he sings, Oscar Peterson.
That's right, yeah.

And he had Lou Donaldson on alto, so Robert (inaudible) had a drummer named Charlie Hawkins and Charlie Hawkins left Robert (inaudible) and he went over to the Blue Morocco -- then it was called Ann's Red Rose and one night he said, Ches, I want you to hear a young lady sing and it happened to be Nancy Wilson. And at the time she was typing in an office building during the week and working on weekends at Ann's Red Rose.
Well, Pearl Bailey worked at the Blue Morocco, too, in her early days and I worked at the Fat Man's you know when it opened across the street?
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Are you talking about the Fat Man's in the Bronx?
Yeah, that's right, up on Boston Road.
Do you know what happened, listen to them --
With 88 Keys --

Well, wait a minute, do you know a piano player named Gene, I used to sing with him. Listen, one night I was singing at the bar for kicks -- I'm not lying, and we had a beer glass and when we got finished we had a lot of dollar bills in there.
Would this Gene be Gene Rogers? I worked with Gene Rogers the night before last up in Larchmont.
He's still around?
Yeah, he's working with the Harlem Blues and Brass Band. I tell you all these guys up there, every one of them was over 70 years old.
Well, I'm getting ready.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Do you know what year that was that I sang with him? 1943, 37 years ago. When he comes on with how long ago -- 1943.
(Laughter)
I mean that's late for me, but -- what's his name again, Gene Rogers?
Gene Rogers, sure.
